newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyz exchange mulls secondary T-bills in March.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyz exchange mulls secondary T-bills in March.

text.p: The Kyrgyz Stock Exchange may start trading national Treasury bills on the secondary market starting next month, the head of the exchange said on Monday.
"The establishment of a liquid T-bill market is in the interests of all participants of the market," Chinarbek Otunchiyev told Reuters.
He said that experimental deals with T-bills on the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange were held last August.
T-bills currently trade in an interbank market where volumes may be higher than those of issues placed at regular auctions held every Thursday.
Nurlan Tynayev, a National Bank department chief, said weekly volumes of T-bill deals on the interbank market reaches 15-20 million som, and annualised yields average 48-50 percent.
The average annual yield on three-month T-bills was 46.91 percent at a primary auction last Thursday.
Tynayev said companies' taxes on securities operations had been lowered to five percent from 15 percent. Private persons are exempt from those taxes.

Otunchiyev said the secondary T-bill market would make it easier for private persons and Kyrgyz institutional investors or companies to sell T-bills before maturity, which now can only be done with difficulty on the interbank market.
